title: NYSDEC project codes
purpose: Map a client project and its field/laboratory QC matrices to explicit NYSDEC recipient codes.
summary: Map a client project and its sample and laboratory QC matrices to the NYSDEC codes its exports need. The codes are reused for every export of the project's released reports.

tasks.title: Set a project's NYSDEC codes
steps: Enter the registered company, laboratory and task codes.
Enter the matrix codes for normal samples and for laboratory QC.

good_to_know: You can save blank fields. The export check tells you which codes the actual data needs.
New codes don't change existing exports or issued reports. Generate a new export to use them.
The codes are not checked against the recipient's reference tables.

sections.title: Access and scope
paragraphs: Project managers, approvers, users with explicit release authority and operational admins can configure and generate EDDs. Other internal roles can read EDD checks but cannot save settings or generate files. Client accounts cannot open these staff pages.

Exploratory NYSDEC chemistry EDD v5 input, format 5.0.0.079 with reference values 20260429. The application checks only its known required fields, lengths, numeric/date formats, enumerations and keys. It does not contain recipient reference tables or validate those codes. Load generated files into EQuIS EDP, resolve its errors, and use EDP’s signing/submission process. No recipient acceptance or compliance is claimed.

The subject identifies client and project. One project’s settings are reused for new exports of all its released report versions. All fields may be saved blank; the export checker identifies values needed by the actual data.

EDD preview blocks text values beginning with =, +, -, @, a tab or a carriage return because a spreadsheet may interpret them as formulas. Saving settings does not bypass that check. The export never rewrites values; use accurate source values and recipient codes. Negative numbers in numeric columns remain allowed.

items.label: Data provider
items.description: Registered submitting-party rt_company code, maximum 20 characters.

items.label: Sampling company code
items.description: Registered field-sampling company rt_company code, maximum 40 characters.

items.label: Lab name code
items.description: Registered code for this laboratory, maximum 20 characters. Also identifies the sampler company for lab-generated QC.

items.label: Task code
items.description: Not set or one of SC, RD, RIFS, RC, IRM, SM, RSO; choose the intended project phase rather than guessing.

items.label: Water matrix code
items.description: Explicit rt_matrix code for this project’s normal water samples, maximum 10 characters. Surface water and groundwater need different recipient codes.

items.label: Wastewater matrix code
items.description: Explicit rt_matrix code for normal wastewater samples, maximum 10 characters.

items.label: Soil matrix code
items.description: Explicit rt_matrix code for normal soil samples, maximum 10 characters.

items.label: Water qc matrix code
items.description: LAB-class rt_matrix for laboratory QC of water batches, maximum 10 characters; distinct from normal-sample code.

items.label: Wastewater qc matrix code
items.description: LAB-class code for wastewater-batch QC, maximum 10 characters.

items.label: Soil qc matrix code
items.description: LAB-class code for soil-batch QC, maximum 10 characters.

sections.title: Saving and navigation
paragraphs: Validation errors retain entered fields. Settings are shared configuration, not a per-export override. There is no stale-edit warning for these forms: coordinate concurrent edits and reload before replacing another person’s changes. Recipient codes are stripped of surrounding whitespace but are not looked up or inferred.

items.label: Save changes
items.description: Validate and audit the entered codes, then return to the originating same-host check/preview when supplied, otherwise Reports. Existing exports and issued reports are unchanged; regenerate an export to use new settings.
